Answer: B
Reason: The frontal chest X-ray (Figure 4a) shows a large anterior mediastinal mass that obscures the right heart border and hilum, demonstrating the "hilum-overlay sign" which is characteristic of anterior mediastinal masses. There are also bibasal pleural effusions visible as blunting of the costophrenic angles and meniscus signs. This constellation of findings—anterior mediastinal mass with pleural effusions—is highly suggestive of an invasive thymic epithelial tumor like thymic carcinoma with pleural metastases.
